title: Count the calls
description:
Write a decorator `count_calls` that counts how many times the decorated function has been called. The count is kept on the wrapper as an attribute named `calls`, starting at 0. The function's result, name and docstring must be unchanged.

```python
@count_calls
def square(x):
    """Squares x."""
    return x * x

square(3)
square(4)
print(square.calls)       # 2
print(square.__name__)    # square
```
hints: A function is an object, so it can carry attributes: set `wrapper.calls = 0` after defining `wrapper`, and inside it do `wrapper.calls += 1`.
Accept and pass on any arguments with `def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): ... return func(*args, **kwargs)`, and put `@functools.wraps(func)` above it.
